# Publish-ZbxDashboard

## SYNOPSIS

Creates or updates a dashboard from a document.

## SYNTAX

### Path (Default)

```
Publish-ZbxDashboard [-Path] <string[]> [-PassThru] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Text

```
Publish-ZbxDashboard -Document <object> [-PassThru] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### LiteralPath

```
Publish-ZbxDashboard -LiteralPath <string[]> [-PassThru] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Publish-ZbxDashboard cmdlet reads a dashboard document, JSON text, files (-Path, which takes wildcards, or -LiteralPath) or an object with the same fields as New-ZbxDashboard's request, and makes the server hold it: a dashboard with the document's name is updated in place with dashboard.update, otherwise one is created with dashboard.create. A script can keep its dashboards as files and publish them again after every change. It writes the dashboard only with -PassThru, and -WhatIf shows what it would do.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Publish a dashboard from JSON text

```powershell
'{"name":"Ops overview","pages":[{"widgets":[{"type":"problems","x":0,"y":0,"width":36,"height":5}]}]}' |
    Publish-ZbxDashboard -PassThru | Select-Object DashboardId, Name
```

The document names the dashboard and its pages; each widget has a type, a position and a size.

### Example 2: Publish a dashboard kept as a file

```powershell
$folder = New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "dashboards-$PID") -Force
'{"name":"Ops overview","pages":[{"widgets":[{"type":"clock","x":0,"y":0,"width":12,"height":3}]}]}' | Set-Content (Join-Path $folder 'ops.json')
Publish-ZbxDashboard -LiteralPath (Join-Path $folder 'ops.json')
```

-LiteralPath reads the document from a file; publishing it again after a change updates the same dashboard.
